tools.name: create_facade_grid
tools.description:
Generate a curtain-wall grid (glass plane + mullions + transoms) on one facade.

    Call it once per facade of a mass (axis "x" or "y" plus outward 1/-1 picks the side).
    The grid is massing-level: one glass plane recessed behind a frame of vertical mullions
    and horizontal transoms, one box per mullion/transom.

    Args:
        origin_x, origin_y, origin_z: corner of the facade plane in mm (bottom-left)
        width: facade length along `axis`, mm
        height: facade height, mm
        axis: "x" or "y" — the direction the facade runs
        outward: 1 or -1 — the side the frame protrudes toward
        bays: bays (vertical divisions) along the facade
        floors: floors (horizontal divisions)
        mullion_width: vertical mullion width, mm
        transom_height: horizontal transom height, mm
        frame_depth: how far the frame protrudes from the plane, mm
        glass_inset: how far glass is recessed behind the frame, mm
        glass_preset: material preset, one of glass_dark, glass_mid, glass_light
        frame_preset: material preset, one of frame_white, frame_light_gray, metal_gray,
            panel_dark, panel_wood, stone_light, concrete

tools.name: create_floor_stack
tools.description:
Generate a stack of floor slabs plus the roof slab for one footprint.

    Use it for exposed floor bands (podium roofs, terraces, parking decks). For a glass
    tower the transoms of create_facade_grid already read as floor lines.

    Args:
        origin_x, origin_y, origin_z: footprint corner in mm
        width, depth: footprint size in mm
        floors: number of floors (a slab is created at every level, roof included)
        floor_height: floor-to-floor height in mm
        slab_thickness: slab thickness in mm
        overhang: how far each slab projects beyond the footprint, mm
        material_preset: material preset (see create_facade_grid for the list)

tools.name: create_exterior
tools.description:
Build a whole building exterior from one parameter spec, then report what to check.

    Fill the spec from the reference image, call this once per attempt, capture the view and
    compare it with the image against the returned checklist. Iterate by editing the spec and
    calling again — never by moving single boxes.

    Spec: {"elements": [...], "camera": {"eye": [x, y, z], "target": [x, y, z]}} with elements
    - tower: x, y, width, depth, floors, floor_height, bays_x, bays_y, crown, base_ring_z,
      glass_preset, frame_preset
    - podium: x, y, width, depth, floors, floor_height, bays, glazed_ground, parapet,
      band_height, solid_preset, frame_preset, glass_preset
    - ribbon_block: x, y, width, depth, floors, floor_height, ribbon_levels, bays,
      panel {width, height, offset_x}, glass_preset, solid_preset
    - colonnade: x_start, y, count, spacing, size, height, preset

tools.name: place_component

Place a furniture component from the component library.

        rotation: Rotation angle in degrees

tools.name: apply_material
tools.description:
Apply material to entities.

    Args:
        entity_ids: List of entity IDs to apply material to
        color: Hex color (e.g., "#C67B5C") or RGB array [r, g, b]
        material_id: Optional SketchUp material name
        preset: Exterior material preset; sets the color unless `color` is given.
            One of: glass_dark, glass_mid, glass_light, frame_white, frame_light_gray,
            metal_gray, stone_light, panel_dark, panel_wood, concrete
        texture_scale_x: Texture scale X in mm
        texture_scale_y: Texture scale Y in mm

tools.name: apply_style
tools.description:
Apply a complete style preset to the model or specific entities.

    Args:
        style_name: Style preset name.
                    Options: "japandi_cream", "modern_industrial", "scandinavian",
                             "mediterranean", "bohemian", "contemporary_minimalist"
        entity_ids: Optional list of entity IDs to apply style to.
                    If None, applies to all faces in the model.

tools.name: search_sketchfab_models
tools.description:
Search Sketchfab for 3D models.

    Use this to find furniture, fixtures, and decorative objects from
    Sketchfab's library of Creative Commons licensed 3D models.

    Args:
        query: Search query (e.g., "modern sofa", "floor lamp", "potted plant")
        count: Number of results to return (max 50)
        sort: Sort order - "relevance", "newest", "likes", "views"

    Returns:
        List of matching 3D models with download links and metadata.

tools.name: get_sketchfab_model
tools.description:
Get detailed information about a Sketchfab model.

    Args:
        model_uid: Sketchfab model UID (from search results)

    Returns:
        Detailed model information including download formats and links.

tools.name: download_sketchfab_model
tools.description:
Download a Sketchfab 3D model.

    Downloads the model in the specified format (OBJ recommended for SketchUp).
    After download, models can be imported into SketchUp.

    Args:
        model_uid: Sketchfab model UID (from search results)
        format_hint: Preferred format - "obj" (recommended for SketchUp), "gltf", "glb"
        output_dir: Output directory (defaults to ~/SketchUp/SCC/downloaded_models/)

    Returns:
        Download status and file path.

tools.name: search_and_download_sketchfab
tools.description:
Search Sketchfab and download the top result in one step.

    Convenience function that searches for models and downloads the
    first downloadable result.

    Args:
        query: Search query (e.g., "minimalist coffee table")
        format_hint: Preferred format - "obj" (recommended for SketchUp), "gltf", "glb"

    Returns:
        Search results and download status.

tools.name: search_warehouse
tools.description:
Get a SketchUp 3D Warehouse search URL.

    Opens the 3D Warehouse search page in your browser where you can
    browse and download 3D models.

    Note: 3D Warehouse does not have a public API, so this tool provides
    a search URL that you can open in your browser.

    Args:
        query: Search query (e.g., "modern sofa", "floor lamp")

    Returns:
        URL to open in browser for searching 3D Warehouse.

tools.name: download_from_warehouse
tools.description:
Get guidance for downloading a model from SketchUp 3D Warehouse URL.

    Note: 3D Warehouse does not have a public API. This tool provides
    guidance for the manual download process.

    Args:
        warehouse_url: Full URL to a 3D Warehouse model page
                       (e.g., https://3dwarehouse.sketchup.com/model/abc123/...)

    Returns:
        Instructions for downloading the model.

tools.name: get_warehouse_model_info
tools.description:
Extract model information from a SketchUp 3D Warehouse URL.

    Note: 3D Warehouse does not have a public API. This tool does
    best-effort extraction of model ID from the URL pattern.

    Args:
        warehouse_url: Full URL to a 3D Warehouse model page

    Returns:
        Model ID and URL extracted from the link.
